chunks: And from him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The fasting person may use the siwak (tooth-stick) at any time of the day he wishes."
ai.seo_question: Does using a tooth-stick (siwak) break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that using the siwak does not invalidate the fast, addressing early juristic debates on whether oral actions affect fasting validity. It underscores the Prophetic tradition of maintaining oral hygiene during Ramadan, emphasizing that the siwak is a recommended act of worship that can be performed at any time during daylight hours without breaking the fast.
